summary.text: A 50-year-old dark-skinned woman with Graves’ disease with hyperthyroidism (diagnosed in 2014) and Addison’s disease presented to a stomatology service with two dark patches on the upper lip mucosa that had grown in recent months with slight itching. Examination showed brown and black patches and plaques on the upper lip mucosa, gingiva, tongue and buccal mucosa, none on the skin.

Mucosal pigmentation associated with Addison’s disease was initially hypothesized, but because of the lack of skin pigmentation, distinct clinical appearance and recent growth, the upper lip lesions were biopsied. Histopathology and HMB-45 immunohistochemistry were consistent with and confirmed oral melanoacanthoma.

At the time of the report she was using Tapazol 5 mg for hyperthyroidism with follow-up assessments every 3 months. No medication for Addison’s disease had been started, and cortisol was within the normal range. The pigmented lesions showed no change in clinical appearance during follow-up.
